raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Export Qwen GDN prefill checkpoints directly from the Triton/FLA chunk recurrence
into the paged state cache. In Mamba `align` mode, this avoids stopping a prefill
at its last cache boundary and avoids rerunning its tail.

## Claims

- Triton/FLA prefill reads initial state and writes final state in the paged
  cache, removing per-layer gather/scatter and masked state initialization.
- The recurrence stores the checkpoint at a 64-token chunk boundary; the shared
  Mamba exporter supplies its convolution window. Autotune replays preserve the
  input cache rows, and warmup covers representative sequence-count buckets.
- Full GSM8K A/B and prefix-hit continuation checks cover standard decoding,
  MTP, and checkpoint reuse. Scores and performance tradeoffs are below.

## Validation

Baseline `7fc467825d`, 2x NVIDIA H20-3e, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP2,
Triton/FLA, prefix caching enabled, block size 1600, 8192-token step budget.
PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, driver 580.105.08; both source checkouts
share precompiled extension artifacts from `7b1d07440d`.

| GSM8K configuration | Baseline | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1319 questions, 8-shot, greedy, thinking off | 1278/1319 (96.89%) | 1278/1319 (96.89%) |
| Same, MTP with 3 speculative tokens | 1276/1319 (96.74%) | 1274/1319 (96.59%) |
| 12-shot with checkpoint hits (~63% hit rate), two runs | 1272, 1271 / 1319 (mean 96.40%) | 1267, 1274 / 1319 (mean 96.32%) |

Standard decoding and MTP have one matched run each. In the two cached runs,
the changed score varies by seven questions and averages one question below
baseline. Invalid-answer rate was zero throughout; MTP accepted draft tokens.

Eight prefix-hit continuation cases per configuration cover English/random-token
prompts, lengths 3000/8000, two seeds, and up to 32 generated tokens with top-5
logprobs. All have the expected 1600/6400 cached tokens and pass the repository's
`check_logprobs_close` comparison. Full-model FP8 outputs are not bitwise equal:
an unchanged-upstream control also changes greedy tokens when primer batching
changes. Kernel and exported-state tests retain exact assertions.

| H20 test group | Result |
| --- | --- |
| FLA suite, GDN metadata, checkpoint exporter, align scheduler | 1839 passed |
| GDN kernel suite | 48 passed, 19 platform skips |
| Model-runner checkpoint grid / block size | 14 passed |
| Mamba prefix-cache e2e (MRV1/MRV2, async, FlashInfer, Triton) | 6 passed |
| Whole-diff pre-commit | Passed |

The metadata-view regression fails on the preceding implementation because an
offset view recompiles the warmed chunk kernel; it passes after excluding
scalar metadata pointers from alignment specialization. A one-variable probe
reduces six metadata-view JIT events from one each to zero, preserving exact
outputs/cache contents. The changed recurrence has no request-time JIT warnings
in either serving benchmark pass.

Changed accuracy servers ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. B200 and MI355 were not
available locally; the existing FLA CI step and the H200/MI355 large-memory e2e
steps select the new tests.

### Serving performance

Two interleaved passes on the same allocated pair of H20s, 8000 input / 128
output tokens, 16/32/128 requests at concurrency 1/4/16, no prefix hits. Fresh
server and warmup per arm/pass; block size explicitly fixed to 1600 in both.

| Concurrency | Mean TTFT ms, baseline → PR | TTFT change | Mean TPOT ms, baseline → PR | Output tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 708.6 → 672.6 | -5.1% | 6.29 → 6.24 | +3.0% |
| 4 | 1955.2 → 1620.4 | -17.1% | 13.29 → 15.23 | +2.5% |
| 16 | 3882.8 → 3375.2 | -13.1% | 61.84 → 65.22 | +0.7% |

TPOT increases by 14.6% at concurrency 4 and 5.5% at 16 on this short-output
workload, despite lower TTFT and slightly higher throughput. This is a latency
tradeoff, not a decode-kernel speedup. At concurrency 16, the two run means are
3852.6/3912.9 ms for baseline and 3375.9/3374.5 ms for the PR. Every request
completed successfully.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/fla \
  tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba -k gdn -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py \
  -k 'checkpoint_grid or block_size' -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py -v

.venv/bin/vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --gdn-prefill-backend triton \
  --enable-prefix-caching --block-size 1600 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --generation-config vllm
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 8 --max-tokens 1024 \
  --use-chat-completions --temperature 0 --seed 42 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' \
  --max-concurrency 16 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

Use `--num-shots 12` for the cached run; add
`--speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'` to the
server for MTP. Use the same flags on both revisions. GPU work ran through Slurm.

For the performance server, omit `--max-num-seqs 16` and `--generation-config
vllm` above (default sequence limit 512), use port 8199, warm up with 8 random
8000/32-token prompts at concurrency 4 and seed 7, then run:

```bash
.venv/bin/vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --port 8199 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8000 \
  --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos --num-prompts "$N" \
  --max-concurrency "$C" --request-rate inf --seed "$SEED" \
  --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir "$RESULT_DIR"
```

Use `(C,N,SEED) = (1,16,101), (4,32,104), (16,128,116)`; repeat with fresh
servers in main/PR/main/PR order.

</details>

## Details

- **Overlap:** #60659 implements the same Triton checkpoint goal using host-side
  row splitting and a second chunk pipeline over the tails, and also covers
  AITER FlyDSL. This is a materially different kernel implementation: direct
  paged-state I/O plus a checkpoint store, with no tail rerun. FlyDSL is outside
  this change. The implementation difference is documented in
  [the existing discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60659#issuecomment-6581991861).
  #64498/#64625 concern FlashInfer state-pool access instead.
- **Reuse:** uses the checkpoint declaration/grid and shared exporter introduced
  for FlashInfer in #60050; generic scheduler/cache-manager interfaces stay as
  they are. Preserves current upstream int64 indexing and FlashInfer output I/O.
- **Tradeoffs:** internal checkpoints reserve one checkpoint block and can reduce
  effective KV capacity. The 64-token grid must be supported by every Mamba
  layer in the model. CUDA and ROCm use this path; XPU retains gather/scatter.
- **Configuration:** `additional_config["gdn_prefill_checkpoint"]` defaults to
  true; false restores split prefill while retaining direct Triton state I/O.
  Usage and the default are documented in Automatic Prefix Caching.
- AI assistance: Claude Code implemented the initial kernel/integration and
  experiments; Codex consolidated the changes, updated upstream compatibility,
  documented the behavior, and ran the validation above.

 ## Hybrid Mamba models
 
+### GDN prefill checkpoints
+
+With prefix caching enabled and `--mamba-cache-mode align`, Qwen Gated DeltaNet
+(GDN) layers can export an internal prefill checkpoint. This lets a prefill
+continue past the cache block boundary in one forward pass, while preserving
+the state needed by a later prefix-cache hit.
+
+Internal checkpoints are enabled by default for the FlashInfer GDN prefill
+backend and for the Triton/FLA backend on CUDA and ROCm. The Triton/FLA kernel
+reads and writes recurrent state directly in the paged cache and exports
+checkpoints on its 64-token chunk grid. Every Mamba layer in a hybrid model
+must support internal checkpoints for this optimization to take effect.
+
+The checkpoint's offset from the start of the current prefill must be a
+multiple of 64; the total prompt length need not be. If the scheduler cannot
+place a valid internal checkpoint, it uses the split prefill path.
+
+To select Triton/FLA explicitly:

+```bash
+vllm serve <qwen-gdn-model> \
+    --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \
+    --gdn-prefill-backend triton

+checkpoint state can also reduce effective KV cache capacity.
+

+GDN checkpoints and restore the split prefill. The Triton/FLA backend still
+uses direct paged-state I/O when checkpoints are disabled.
+
+### Shared-prefix junction checkpoints
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Paged-state I/O and mid-sequence checkpoints of the FLA chunk kernel.
+
+The paged cache is a strided view whose rows sit inside wider pages, as in
+vLLM's hybrid KV cache, so a contiguous copy anywhere on the way would silently
+drop the in-place writes.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import chunk_gated_delta_rule
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.chunk_delta_h import (
+    chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64,
+)
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+DEVICE = current_platform.device_type
+NUM_K_HEADS, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM = 2, 4, 128
+ROW_SIZE = NUM_V_HEADS * HEAD_DIM * HEAD_DIM
+NUM_SLOTS = 12
+
+
+def _make_inputs(seq_lens: list[int]) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+    num_tokens = sum(seq_lens)
+    q, k = (
+        F.normalize(
+            torch.randn(1, num_tokens, NUM_K_HEADS, HEAD_DIM), dim=-1
+        ).bfloat16()
+        for _ in range(2)
+    )
+    v = torch.randn(1, num_tokens, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM).bfloat16()
+    g = F.logsigmoid(torch.randn(1, num_tokens, NUM_V_HEADS))
+    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(1, num_tokens, NUM_V_HEADS))
+    return q, k, v, g, beta
+
+
+def _cu_seqlens(seq_lens: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.tensor([0, *seq_lens]).cumsum(0).to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _make_pages(dtype: torch.dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Each page holds one state row followed by padding, like a Mamba page
+    # padded to the attention page size.
+    return (0.1 * torch.randn(NUM_SLOTS, ROW_SIZE + 96)).to(dtype)
+
+
+def _state_rows(pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return pages[:, :ROW_SIZE].view(NUM_SLOTS, NUM_V_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM)
+
+
+def _run(inputs: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], seq_lens: list[int], **kwargs):
+    q, k, v, g, beta = inputs
+    return chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+        q=q, k=k, v=v, g=g, beta=beta, cu_seqlens=_cu_seqlens(seq_lens), **kwargs
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_equal(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    # Exact: the variants compute every element the same way, whatever
+    # autotune config each picks.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("state_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_state_cache_matches_gathered_states(
+    state_dtype: torch.dtype, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    """In-place paged state I/O equals gathering and scattering the rows.
+
+    The sequences end mid-chunk, on a chunk boundary and after one token. One
+    starts fresh from a row holding stale values; row 0 (NULL_BLOCK_ID) is
+    neither read nor written, so that sequence also starts from zero. The rows
+    come as a strided block-table column. The
+    in-place launch is autotuned afresh, which replays it once per config and
+    benchmark repetition: each replay must start from the same rows. vLLM
+    caches autotuning on disk, so without a fresh in-process cache only a cold
